note: UPGRADED FROM THE FALLBACK: this table now ships the ADMINISTERED POLISH. It originally shipped English in the base fields as translated_substitute, on the finding that the Polish was in neither the deposit nor the paper. It is in neither -- but it IS in the Polish adaptation the paper cites, Grzesiak-Feldman (2012), whose Zalacznik 1 lists a 20-item 'Skala Prawicowego Autorytaryzmu'. All twelve items this study administered appear there verbatim. So Polish takes item_text, the .sav's English labels move to item_text_translated (the authors' own renderings, hence translation_source=study_supplied), and text_source becomes study_materials. THE PAIRING IS FORCED BY CONTENT, not position: each of the twelve English labels is a direct translation of exactly one numbered appendix item and vice versa, drawn from a pool of twenty. The map is rwa1<-13, rwa2<-2, rwa3<-8, rwa4<-4, rwa5<-9, rwa6<-1, rwa7<-14, rwa8<-7, rwa9<-12, rwa10<-6, rwa11<-11, rwa12<-3, so the study used appendix items 1-4, 6-9 and 11-14 and none of 5, 10 or 15-20. CORRECTS A CLAIM THIS TABLE ORIGINALLY SHIPPED. Its first public note said the items are 'stored RAW'. They are not. Solving for the weights of the deposit's own rwa_sum returns +1 on all twelve with a zero intercept, reproducing it for 342 of 342 complete rows; flipping the six reverse-worded items instead reproduces only 22 of 342. So the deposit stores them ALREADY RECODED, with higher meaning more authoritarian for every item. A consequence worth stating: keying polarity therefore cannot be used to test the pairing on this table -- all twelve intercorrelate positively, across-block r = +0.160 rather than negative -- and that is explained by the recoding rather than being a failure of the mapping. RESPONSE ANCHORS STILL NOT SHIPPED, and the new source is the reason to be careful rather than bolder: the appendix publishes a SIX-point scale ('(1) Zdecydowanie sie nie zgadzam' through '(6) Zdecydowanie sie zgadzam'), but this study administered FIVE points -- the paper says 5-point and the live data contains only 1-5. So the appendix's labels do not describe this administration and option_text stays blank.

source_ref: Deposit workbook 'Knowledge and Fear of COVID-19 and Perceived Stress.xlsb' (osf.io/m2v3h) -- its 'Codebook' sheet keys Q1..Q12 to their statements and states '0 - Incorrect; 1 - Correct', its 'Survey 1' sheet carries the same twelve statements with the True/False answer key and a % Correct column, and its 'DataSet' sheet holds the response columns; data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' for the code derivation. Article: Li & Leung (2020), Data in Brief 33:106395, CC BY, PMC7546663.
note: BARE-INTEGER ITEM CODES THAT ARE NOT ACTUALLY OPAQUE. The live codes are 1-12, which normally demands reconstruction caution, but the .do file reshapes `Q1 Q2 ... Q12 -> Q` and renames the reshape index to `item`, so the integer IS the Q number; the Codebook sheet then keys each Q to its statement. The mapping is mechanical, not inferred. TWO SHEETS CROSS-CHECK EACH OTHER: the Codebook and Survey 1 statements are byte-identical for 11 of the 12, and the twelfth is recoverable only from Survey 1 because the Codebook's Q4 cell is a broken spreadsheet reference rendering as '0x17'. That item is 'Only those who are elderly, have chronic illnesses, and/ or are obese could suffer severe symptoms as a result of COVID-19.' EXTRACTION NOTE: the deposit is an Excel BINARY workbook (.xlsb), which openpyxl cannot read and no office converter was available; it was read positionally with pyxlsb. An earlier attempt that harvested UTF-16 strings out of the raw sheet bytes silently lost this same Q4 item, so the positional read matters. WHAT resp MEANS, and this is the thing a user must not misread: respondents chose among THREE options, 'True, false, I don't know', but the live table does not store that choice. It stores CORRECTNESS, 0 = Incorrect and 1 = Correct, per the Codebook sheet. So option_text labels the stored values and not what anyone selected, and correct_response is 1 for every item by construction. The substantive answer key, which is what the item is actually asserting, is: 1 - True; 2 - True; 3 - True; 4 - False; 5 - False; 6 - False; 7 - True; 8 - True; 9 - False; 10 - True; 11 - True; 12 - True. VERIFICATION: the workbook publishes % Correct per item, and the observed proportion of resp == 1 reproduces all twelve to 0.000e+00 -- see verify_kfcovid_Li2020.R. Instrument provenance: the article says the twelve were 'adapted from' Zhong et al. (2020), Int J Biol Sci 16:1745, so the wording shipped here is this study's own as deposited, not Zhong's.
public_note: Twelve true/false COVID-19 knowledge statements. IMPORTANT: resp is not the respondent's answer. Respondents chose True, false, or 'I don't know', and the table stores only whether they were right -- 0 = Incorrect, 1 = Correct -- so correct_response is 1 throughout. Whether each statement is itself true or false is: 1 - True; 2 - True; 3 - True; 4 - False; 5 - False; 6 - False; 7 - True; 8 - True; 9 - False; 10 - True; 11 - True; 12 - True. Item codes are the source workbook's Q numbers. n = 110 Filipino domestic workers in Hong Kong, July 2020.

source_ref: Deposit osf.io/mvdpe, folder '6. Measures' -- Codebook_Baseline.xlsx rows 124-137 carry all fourteen items with a per-item response ladder in its Values column; data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r line 61 for the code derivation. Preprint: Fried & Epskamp (2022), 'Mental Health and Social Contact During the COVID-19 Pandemic: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study', doi:10.31234/osf.io/36xkp, deposit CC BY. SAS-SV source: Kwon, Kim, Cho & Yang (2013), PLoS ONE 8(12):e83558, CC BY.
note: THE SMARTPHONE BLOCK IS IN THE BASELINE CODEBOOK, NOT THE EMA ONE, which is the first thing to know about this table: the study is an ecological-momentary-assessment design and the deposit ships Codebook_EMA.xlsx, Codebook_Post.xlsx and Codebook_Baseline.xlsx, but searching the EMA codebook for these items returns nothing. All fourteen live here in Baseline. MAPPING is a number-preserving rename with nothing positional in it: the codebook's cleandata_pre column names them Q102..Q115, and data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r calls process_dass_data(bt_df, "Pre", 102, 115, ...) which selects num_range("Pre", 102:115) and pivots with names_to = "item", so the live code is the source column name and its number is the codebook's Q number. TWO BLOCKS, FIVE DIFFERENT LADDERS. Section 1 is the ten-item Smartphone Addiction Scale - Short Version on a single 6-point agree/disagree ladder. Section 2 is four study-specific general-use items, each with its OWN ladder of a different length: duration of use (6), frequency of use (6), time to first use in the morning (4), and function with most personal relevance (8). The codebook's Values cell is populated only on the first row of each block and inherited down, which the extraction handles explicitly. CORROBORATION: every item's observed response range falls inside its own codebook ladder, and the ladder lengths are a distinctive fingerprint -- Pre114 tops out at exactly 4 while Pre112 and Pre115 stop short of their 6 and 8 because two offered levels went unchosen (Pre112 '6 = More than 6 hours' and Pre115 '8 = Reading news'). Those two unused levels are why the live table shows a maximum resp of 7 and why IRW metadata records 7 categories despite one item offering eight. PRE115 IS NOMINAL and this is a data-standard concern rather than an item-text one: its resp values are arbitrary category codes for which smartphone function a respondent named, so they are not ordinal and should not be treated as a scale. The codebook itself marks its measurement level Nominal, unlike every other item here. Ladder parsing note: several option labels contain digits ('11-60 minutes', '6-10 times', 'within 6-30 minutes'), so the ladders were split only at a number matching the next expected level, never at a digit inside a label. RIGHTS: clears the test positively rather than by silence. The SAS-SV was published in PLoS ONE under CC BY with these ten items on a 1 'strongly disagree' to 6 'strongly agree' scale, matching the codebook, and the wording shipped here is transcribed from this study's own CC BY deposit.
public_note: Fourteen smartphone items from the study's BASELINE assessment. Section 1 is the ten-item Smartphone Addiction Scale - Short Version, all on one 6-point ladder from 'Strongly disagree' to 'Strongly agree'. Section 2 is four general-use items and each has a DIFFERENT ladder -- duration of use, frequency of use, time to first morning use, and most-relevant function -- so do not read a shared response scale across this table. IMPORTANT: Pre115 is NOMINAL. Its resp values are category codes for which smartphone function the respondent named (1 = Social networking, 2 = Phoning, 3 = Gaming, and so on), not an ordered scale, and averaging or correlating it would be meaningless. Two offered levels were never chosen and so do not appear: Pre112's '6 = More than 6 hours' and Pre115's '8 = Reading news'.

note: ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, NOT A LITERAL SUM, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE REFUSAL rather than a gap. The deposit ships FOUR parallel forms of this test (Math 3-5_Form1..Form4, plus four '3-5 testing booklet_sample*' booklets) and their content differs -- the four PDFs are pairwise non-identical and their numeral sequences differ. The live table records no form: its columns are cluster_id, wave, cov_female, cov_age, cov_grade, treat, e2_std12, e2_std35, test and item_grade, none of which identifies which booklet a child received. So no literal problem is a property of an item code. The English form that IS readable ('Math 3-5_Mar27_Form1eng.doc', headed 'MATHS (3-5) TEST 1') contains concrete sums -- 36 + 61, 678 + 923, 98 - 55, 238 - 129, 6971 + 5291, 'What is the place value of 9740?' -- and shipping those as item_text would assert content that roughly three quarters of respondents never saw. The task description is what the source ties to the code and it is what ships. CONSEQUENCE a user should expect: item_text repeats across a task family. Five items read 'Multiplication', five 'Solve the sums', four 'Addition(2-3 digit)', four 'Subtraction(2-3 digit)', three each 'Division' and 'Word Problem'. That is the source's granularity, not an extraction failure. MAPPING: live codes are the deposit's variable names with the wave prefix (b_ baseline, e1_/e2_ endline) stripped, and the live `wave` column (0, 0.5, 1) carries what the prefix encoded. The dictionary's 36 codes and the live 36 are the same set exactly. The renaming itself happened upstream of this repo -- data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external 'gilbert_share/06 IL-HTE Econ/analysis/' -- so it was verified from the wave-availability pattern instead; see verify_gilbert_meta_73.R. THE TEST CHANGED BETWEEN WAVES, which is why 11 of the 36 codes are wave-restricted: hvy_obj ('Circle the heaviest object') and sol_a..sol_e ('Solve the sums') are baseline-only, and add3d_c, add3d_d, mul_d, mul_e and subt3d_d are endline-only. Question NUMBERING also differs between the baseline and endline forms because the baseline carried the five extra sol_* items -- add3d_a is q9a at baseline but q8a at endline, division is q15 against q14 -- so no single question number is canonical and none is shipped. RESP: 0/1, and the deposit carries no value labels for these variables, so option_text is blank rather than invented. That 1 means correct is not stated outright but follows from makedata.do recoding 9 to 0 and summing the items into test scores with rowtotal; it is recorded in the public note as an inference, not as a transcription. correct_response is empty because the correct answer is form-dependent and resp is already a correctness score.
public_note: Thirty-six items from the written mathematics test for standards 3-5, pooled across baseline (wave 0), midline (0.5) and endline (1). IMPORTANT: item_text is the TASK the item asks, not the specific sum. note: SHIPPED PARTIAL: STRUCTURE WITHOUT WORDING. No item wording is published for this scale anywhere in the record, so item_text is blank for all twenty -- the .sav labels cons1..cons20 as bare strings 'conservatism item1'..'item20', and the CC BY paper reproduces exactly TWO of the twenty as unkeyed subscale examples: 'The Christian values should be specially protected in Poland.' (social) and 'Currently the richest people pay too high taxes.' (economic). Two of twenty, unkeyed, cannot be assigned to codes. WHAT IS SHIPPED INSTEAD is the subscale each item belongs to, and that is proven rather than inferred. The deposit scores cult_cons and ec_cons; solving for their weights over cons1..cons20 returns weights of exactly 1 on ten items and 0 on the other ten, with a zero intercept, reproducing both composites for all 385 complete rows to a maximum residual of 6.04e-14. THE SCALE ALTERNATES: the odd-numbered items are the cultural/social conservatism subscale and the even-numbered ones are economic conservatism, and the two sets partition all twenty with no overlap. Those are the two sections.
